name: wrong_number_cut

input.source: Bats eat up to 1000 insects in one hour

why: spec/grounding.md worked example: 100 does not normalize to anything in the source's number set ({1000, 1}), so the bullet is cut even though every name in it is fine.

name: wrong_name_cut

input.source: Someone built the shelter using scrap wood

why: 'Zeb' is sentence-initial but not a common word and not in the stoplist, so it is a name candidate; it never appears in the source at all, invented or not.

name: invented_name_carol_vs_alice
why: spec/grounding.md's own example: the invented name is caught even though the source has other capitalized names (Bob), because grounding checks each candidate independently, not just 'some capitalized word matched'.

name: paraphrase_they_for_bats_kept
why: 'They' is sentence-initial and in the stoplist, so it is never a name candidate; a pronoun paraphrase of the subject survives grounding.

name: spelled_out_percent_in_source_kept

input.source: five percent of bats roost in this cave

why: v4 addition: 'five percent' in the source normalizes to '5', matching the bullet's '5%'.

name: thousands_separator_both_sides_kept

input.source: Bats eat up to 1000 insects in one hour

why: spec/grounding.md worked example: 1,000 and 1000 normalize to the same number.

name: reversed_relation_not_caught
why: spec/grounding.md is explicit that this is the failure mode the deterministic filter cannot see: both names and the number are present in the source, so it passes despite the relation being backwards. The graded rubric (spec/eval/grade.md) is what catches this, not grounding.

name: hyphenated_and_lowercase_split_source_form_kept

input.source: A disease called white nose killed many bats

why: spec/grounding.md: a hyphenated candidate is compared on its base AND its hyphen-split parts, so 'White-nose' matches a source that spells it as two separate lowercase words.

name: all_caps_common_acronym_excluded_uncommon_one_kept

input.bullet: The USA and the NPS said OK on TV

why: spec/grounding.md: 2-5 letter all-caps tokens are candidates unless their lowercase form is a common word; spec/common-words.txt actually contains 'usa', 'ok' and 'tv' but not 'nps', so only NPS survives as a candidate here.

name: all_bullets_cut_signal

input.chunkText: Alice paid Bob $5. Dev owes nothing.

why: spec/grounding.md all_cut: when every bullet of a chunk is cut (an invented name in each), groundChunk signals allCut so the caller can show/speak notice.all_cut and offer Read this part.

name: mixed_chunk_one_survivor

input.chunkText: Bats feed at night. Alice paid Bob $5.

why: a chunk with at least one grounded bullet is not all-cut, even though a sibling bullet in the same chunk failed.

name: date_comma_not_a_thousands_separator

input.source: The report came out on May 3, 2026 after a long delay

why: spec/grounding.md (PR #8): a comma joins digits only when exactly three follow it, so the source holds 3 and 2026, not 32026.

name: list_of_numbers_stays_separate
why: spec/grounding.md: '2, 4 and 6' is three numbers; the old run-based regex glued '2, 4' into 24.
